reasoning: Recent polling and forecaster updates show the Idaho Senate race remains strongly Republican, but the dynamic has shifted from an easy R landslide over a Democrat to a much more competitive contest against an independent, even though structural fundamentals are still heavily R+19 statewide. The most recent quantified forecast (within the last 45 days) still shows an R+36–37 type race when framed as a generic R vs D contest, but newer issue and campaign coverage plus prior Achilles polling suggest the realistic current margin in a Risch vs Achilles general election is far smaller, roughly an R+4 to R+8 environment, with Republicans clearly favored but no longer at their earlier near-lock odds. No credible recent presidential polling or forecasting specific to Idaho in the last 45 days appears in the search results, so the current margin assessment applies to the 2026 Senate race only.

sources.name: PredictionHunt summary of Peak Insights poll
sources.details: Peak Insights statewide poll found Sen. Jim Risch at 55%, Democrat David Roth at 15%, with independents Todd Achilles at 7% and Natalie Fleming at 5%, and Libertarian Matt Loesby at 2%, implying about an R+40 lead over the nearest major opponent at that time.

sources.name: PollsMax 2026 Idaho Senate Forecast
sources.details: PollsMax’s Idaho Senate forecast, last updated July 12, 2026, projects a general election result of 68.4% R vs 31.6% D with an R+36.8 projected margin and a polling-average margin of R+36.0 based on the Peak Insights survey.

sources.name: ABC45 report on Achilles-sponsored Idaho Senate poll
sources.details: An Achilles-sponsored poll cited by ABC45 reported independent Todd Achilles within four points of Risch, with Achilles 4 points behind the senator and nearly a quarter of voters undecided, indicating roughly an R+4 race in that independent vs Republican framing.

sources.name: The Downballot summary of Bullfinch Group Idaho Senate polling
sources.details: The Downballot’s Morning Digest reports a Bullfinch Group poll showing Risch leading Achilles 40–36 in a hypothetical one‑on‑one matchup (R+4) and Risch ahead 41–18–15 in a three‑way with Achilles and Roth, while a two‑way Risch–Roth ballot had Risch up 50–33 (R+17).

sources.name: Roll Call on Idaho Democrat dropping out in Senate race
sources.details: Roll Call reports that Democratic Senate nominee David Roth has dropped out of the Idaho race, following a strategy used in other red states, and that independent Todd Achilles is now the main challenger to Republican Sen. Jim Risch, signaling a consolidated non‑Republican field but still a challenging environment.

sources.name: PredictionHunt coverage of Idaho Senate betting odds move
sources.details: PredictionHunt reports that despite Risch’s 40‑point polling lead over Roth in June, betting markets have repriced Idaho’s Senate race, with the Republican win probability dropping from 97% to 67% over three days, indicating betting sentiment that the race is still strongly but not absolutely Republican‑favored.
sources.date_range: July 20, 2026 (article summarizing June 7 poll and recent market moves)

sources.name: PredictionHunt on Idaho Senate market repricing
sources.details: A separate PredictionHunt piece details a collapse in implied Republican odds in the Idaho Senate market from 97% to 66% over three days, noting that all major forecasters still rate Idaho "Solid R" and referencing Risch’s large polling leads over Democratic opponents.

sources.name: PredictionEdge Idaho Senate winner‑by‑party odds
sources.details: PredictionEdge’s Idaho Senate winner‑by‑party page shows Republicans with about a 93% chance of winning and Democrats at about 1%, reflecting a heavily but not absolutely secure Republican position in structural and probabilistic models.

sources.name: Cook Political Report statewide PVI for Idaho
sources.details: The Cook Political Report’s Partisan Voting Index rates Idaho as R+19 statewide, indicating the state votes roughly 19 points more Republican than the national average in recent presidential elections and providing the key structural context for interpreting 2026 Senate polling and forecasts.
sources.date_range: Cook PVI (baseline, not a race poll)
